primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Loss of tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase activity from pathogenic ALPL variants prevents normal hydrolysis of inorganic pyrophosphate, allowing extracellular pyrophosphate to accumulate and inhibit hydroxyapatite crystal growth and bone/tooth mineralization.
vignette: A 5-year-old boy is evaluated for bowed legs, bone pain, and premature loss of several primary teeth with intact roots. Radiographs show poorly mineralized bone. Serum alkaline phosphatase activity is persistently low. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in ALPL.
lead: Accumulation of which of the following substrates most directly contributes to the defective skeletal mineralization in this patient?
distractor_notes: Homogentisic acid accumulates in alkaptonuria and causes ochronosis rather than low-alkaline-phosphatase defective mineralization.
Oxalate accumulation causes calcium oxalate deposition, nephrolithiasis, and systemic oxalosis rather than hypophosphatasia.
Methylmalonic acid accumulates in methylmalonic acidemia and does not explain the ALPL-associated mineralization defect.
Homocysteine accumulation occurs in homocystinuria and causes vascular, ocular, and connective-tissue manifestations rather than low ALP with root-intact tooth loss.
key_expl: ALPL encodes tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase, which has inorganic pyrophosphate as a natural substrate. In hypophosphatasia, deficient enzyme activity permits extracellular pyrophosphate accumulation. Pyrophosphate inhibits hydroxyapatite crystal growth, producing defective mineralization of bone and teeth.
objective: Connect ALPL/tissue-nonspecific alkaline-phosphatase deficiency with inorganic pyrophosphate accumulation and impaired hydroxyapatite mineralization in hypophosphatasia.
